## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Hetuduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.1) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the Paṭṭhāna, the seventh and final treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka. It forms part of the Duka-Tika-Paṭṭhāna division, which systematically cross-correlates the dyadic (*duka*) and triadic (*tika*) matrices of the Abhidhamma *mātikā* to examine conditional relations [Nyanatiloka 2007]. In this specific section, the Root Dyad (*hetuduka*) is combined with the Wholesome Triad (*kusalattika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007].

Methodologically, the text examines conditional dependencies across these combined classifications under twenty-four condition types, beginning with the root condition (*hetuppaccaya*) and object condition [Nyanatiloka 2007]. It interrogates combinations of positive and negative determinations; for example, investigating what arises dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and wholesome (*hetuñceva kusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca*), yielding outcomes that may be roots and wholesome, not roots but wholesome, or both [Nyanatiloka 2007]. It also investigates permutations incorporating negative conditionality, such as *nahetuduka-kusalattika* in relation to *hetuduka-kusalattika* [Nyanatiloka 2007].

 Computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse consisting of 610 matching passages across 71 Pali texts, reflecting the highly standardized, formulaic prose of the Paṭṭhāna [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments occur with related combinatorial sections of the Paṭṭhāna, notably *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1; 64 matches), *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 81 matches), *Kusalattika, Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 4.2; 41 matches), and *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2; 50 matches), as well as late Abhidhamma question-and-answer literature such as the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan traditions [DharmaNexus].
